P J Raju vs State Of Kerala on 26 March, 2026

The accused in Crime No.85 of 2025 of Kasaragod Vanitha Police Station filed this Crl.M.C. under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, praying to quash all further proceedings against him.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 376(2)
(n) and 506(i) of the IPC.
2. The prosecution case is that, in January 2002, the accused, after promising to marry the de facto complainant, committed rape upon her.

Thereafter, during the period from October 2010 till April 2012, the accused allegedly committed rape upon the de facto complainant at his residence and intimidated by stating that her nude photographs were available in his mobile phone and that the same would be shown to her husband.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, even if the entire allegations levelled against the petitioner are accepted as true, the CRL.MC NO. 8317 OF 2025 2026:KER:27424 same would only indicate a consensual relationship, and therefore he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent/de facto complainant as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. On a perusal of the FIS, it can be seen that the de facto complainant got married on 03.04.2006.

As per the FI statement, when the defacto complainant was studying in 12th grade, she fell in love with the petitioner and that they could not marry at that time as the petitioner belonged to a different community.
On one day in January 2002, as invited by the petitioner, she went to his residence, and on that day he allegedly committed rape upon her.
Thereafter, the relationship continued at the residence of the petitioner.
In 2004, the petitioner went to Italy in connection with his employment.
On 28.09.2010, he contacted the de facto complainant over telephone, and thereafter their relationship resumed.
As invited by the petitioner, she went to his residence at Kanhangad, and again the relationship continued till April 2012.
On a perusal of the above statement, it is clear that the relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant was a consensual one.
